chunks: And it is narrated from Ṣafwān al-Jammāl, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “I assigned a man an ʿīnah, then it became due upon him, so I said to him: ‘Repay me.’ He said: ‘I do not have it with me, so assign me another ʿīnah until I repay you.’ He said: ‘Assign it to him until he repays you.’”

key_terms.صَفْوَانَ الْجَمَّالِ: Ṣafwān al-Jammāl, the narrator reporting the hadith
key_terms.عِينَةً: a transaction of ʿīnah in this financial context

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to renew an ʿīnah transaction for a debtor who cannot repay when the payment becomes due?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a financial transaction involving ʿīnah and the deferment of repayment when the debtor is unable to pay at maturity. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام permits renewing or specifying the transaction for him until he repays, indicating a jurisprudential ruling in the context of debt and exchange.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4034 - It is narrated from Safwan al-Jammal, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (as): "I appointed a specific loan (aynah) for a man, and it became due. I said to him, 'Repay me.'
He said: 'I do not have it now, so specify another loan for me until I can repay you.'"
Imam (as) said: "Specify it for him until he repays you."
